notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs the intrinsic boundary for excellent local reduction, bounded positive gauge denominators, quotient-first valuation extensions, normalization local centres, finite OPEN singleton fibres and CLOSED quotient fibres at infinity. Completion includes nonminimal supports and primary contraction is exact.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n1: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Let R be an excellent Noetherian local ring, replaced by its reduction, and a a proper m-primary ideal. The boundary contains ALL real semivaluations v with v(a)=1, including nonminimal supports. Nilpotents have value infinity. A zero-dimensional local reduction is a field and has empty boundary.

In [0,infinity]^R, the semivaluation identities and v(m)=1 are closed conditions: extended addition and minimum are continuous, the sum inequality is closed, and finite generation makes v(m) a finite minimum. Thus the m-section is compact Hausdorff. Choose r,s>0 with m^r contained in a contained in m^s. Then s v(m)<=v(a)<=r v(m). Division by v(a) identifies the m-section with the a-section. For primary gauges a,b, the map is v -> v/v(b), and homogeneous functions transform by u_b(v/v(b))=u_a(v)/v(b). The positive continuous denominator is bounded above and below; these transformations preserve uniform closure and actual decreasing nets and satisfy the exact cocycle. Nonprimary ideals provide only partial sections.

Nonemptiness follows from a one-dimensional domain quotient, finite excellent normalization and a DVR at a closed normalization centre. Branches are indexed by normalization local CENTRES, not merely minimal primes.

For a finite injection R -> B with B reduced, every target boundary point has a lift in the FULL source boundary. First quotient by its support p, choose P above p, and extend the valuation through Frac(R/p) -> Frac(B/P). Extending a supportful semivaluation directly to Frac(R) would be invalid. Integral closure, lying over and a maximal dominating local overring produce a valuation ring extension. The maximal-overring argument uses adjoining x or x^{-1}; if the old maximal ideal becomes the unit ideal after adjoining x^{-1}, its equation makes x integral, so adjoining x still permits a dominating prime. Algebraicity makes the new value group a torsion extension of the old one, hence a subgroup of its real divisible hull. Integrality gives nonnegative values. All actual fibres are retained, including vertical components. A zero-dimensional source field factor has aB=0 and contributes no normalized point or invented degree. Compact surjectivity gives the quotient topology.

For finite normalization S, clearing denominators gives a regular conductor element. With c=Ann_R(S/R), one has R=S x_{S/c} R/c: an element of S whose residue comes from R already lies in R. Chinese remainders separate the finitely many local-centre boundary pieces. If v(c)<infinity, choose c with finite value; every lift satisfies w(s)=v(cs)-v(c), proving uniqueness. At v(c)=infinity the fibres are exactly those of (S/c)_red -> (R/c)_red. The finite stratum is OPEN and the infinite stratum CLOSED. Quotient topology descends continuous and upper semicontinuous fibre-constant functions; positivity requires later proofs.

For completion, representatives f_N of F modulo m^N have stable values below N v(m); otherwise their limiting value is infinity. This defines the unique completed semivaluation and proves its identities. Since v(m)>=1/r on the a-section, applying t -> t/(1+t) bounds truncation error by 1/(1+N/r), uniformly. Restriction and extension are inverse homeomorphisms. If completed primary J contains mhat^N, lift its finite image through Rhat/mhat^N=R/m^N. Those lifts and m^N generate J, proving J=(J intersect R)Rhat with proper-primary contraction.

These arguments use ordinary Noetherian and excellence background at its actual hypotheses, not supplied correctness metadata. Full reconstruction: whole-proof.md. Exact input records: exact-input-hashes.json. Rerun integrity with python review_audit.py.

notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n2: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS. Use LOCAL n1.

Let E be Noetherian semilocal, J contain a power of its boundary ideal aE, and w(Q)>=w(J) on every normalized centred semivaluation. Test EVERY minimal component. On each positive-dimensional domain component where J is proper, Swanson--Huneke 6.8.3--4 applies to the centred rank-one DVRs, which are allowed normalized boundary points. Unit components impose no condition. A zero-dimensional component has empty boundary: if J-image is zero, Q-image=0 must be separately required. The later Q=K(aE)^L, L>0, satisfies this because aE vanishes there.

Lift monic integral equations from all minimal components, multiply them and raise their nilpotent product to a power. Coefficients remain in the appropriate J-powers, so Q is integral over J even on nonreduced conductor quotients. This is the immediate proof in book 1.1.5.

A COMMON exponent does not follow merely from pointwise dependence. E[(J+Q)t] is finite over E[Jt], because finitely many Qt-generators are integral. Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most h. In degree N+h every coefficient has at least N J-factors. Therefore Q^(N+h) is contained in (J+Q)^(N+h), which is contained in J^N, for every N>=1. Book 1.2.3--5 supplies the equivalent reduction argument; its integral-closure bars were independently checked in printed PDF page 6.

The complete book 10.2.2 proof, including its 10.2.3 continuation, constructs Rees DVRs through normalized Rees charts and finitely many relevant height-one primes. Its denominator argument brings inequalities back downstairs. Book 10.4.3 gives residue transcendence degree dim(A)-1 at a formally equidimensional local target. Excellence gives universal catenarity, and B.5.1 supplies formal equidimensionality. For a finite-type birational domain chart B0 and P above m, B.3.2 gives dim(B0_P)+trdeg_k kappa(P)=dim A. Its immediate modification of B.2.5 is explicit: catenarity changes ht(Q)+ht(I)<=ht(Q') to equality in the algebraic one-generator step; the transcendental step is already equality, and induction and transcendence-degree additivity finish the argument.

For an excellent NORMAL local domain A, exact Stacks 0C23, Lemma 15.53.6, makes Ahat normal because formal fibres are normal. A complete local normal ring is a domain, so A is analytically irreducible and analytically unramified. This says nothing comparable about arbitrary nonnormal completions. Rond--Spivakovsky v1 Theorem 1.3 consequently applies. Compare a fixed divisorial nu with all m-Rees valuations nu_j: nu(f)<=C0 min_j nu_j(f)/nu_j(m)=C0 barord_m(f). Theorem 1.4 gives barord_m(f)<=ord_m(f)+K. For nonzero nonunits, ord_m(f)>=1, hence nu(f)<=C0(1+K)ord_m(f). Units have both values zero and are handled separately; the literal strict Remark 1.6 cannot be applied to them. Zero has infinite value. Swanson's entire Section 5 was checked, but its complete-domain theorem was not silently promoted to arbitrary domains.

All named immediate proofs and contexts were read. Printed page 140 restores the bars in 6.8.3--4. Historical Rees, Izumi, Ratliff and formal-fibre foundations remain disclosed published dependencies, not recursively fresh proofs. Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n3: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS. Use LOCAL n1.

Q_R consists of finite nonnegative REAL sums of -v(I), for proper primary or unit ideals. C_R is its uniform closure among finite continuous functions. D_R consists of infima of NONEMPTY actual decreasing C_R-NETS, including zero and bottom. On semilocal boundaries, Chinese remainders modulo a common large primary power glue ideals proper at selected centres and unit at others. Empty field factors impose no conditions. Rational coefficient approximation and ideal products make single profiles -v(I)/k dense in C_R. Maxima use I+J; real coefficients follow by uniform approximation. Sums and maxima in D use product directed index sets, without increasing closure, subtraction or unsupported nested-net flattening.

After common denominators, the rational DIFFERENCE span is a lattice because min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH). Constants come from v(a)=1. Truncations (f)+a^N separate boundary points, including coordinates with infinite values. Its UNIFORM closure is a REAL vector lattice, not an integer ideal formula for irrational coefficients. Two-point affine interpolation, finite minima around one point and finite maxima over the compact space prove lattice density in all real continuous functions.

Let A be excellent normal local DOMAIN and B a finite domain A-algebra of field degree n. Choose finite normal M containing all embeddings Sigma of L=Frac(B), and inseparable degree q, so n=q|Sigma|. For generators b_i of a boundary-primary J, its norm polynomial is product_sigma(sum T_i sigma(b_i))^q. Over an algebraic closure each embedding has generic inseparable length q. Coefficients lie in Frac(A) and are integral over A, so normality puts them in A. Their coefficient ideal N(J) is generator-independent by linear substitutions. Pure coefficients x^n for x in a large primary power contained in J show the primary radical condition.

Normalize A in M, obtaining finite E. Lift ANY supportful v to E using n1, and compose with each embedding to obtain w_sigma on B. On the support quotient, minimum coefficient value defines a multiplicative Gauss valuation: nonzero leading residue polynomials have nonzero product. Therefore v(N(J))=q sum_sigma w_sigma(J) on ALL supports. The measure mu_v=q sum_sigma delta_(w_sigma) has mass n. Its ideal-profile moments are intrinsic; density of the full real lattice makes the measure independent of the chosen lift. Every point of the FULL fibre extends from B to E and occurs among these restrictions. Thus every fibre point has positive mass at least 1, and after normalization at least 1/n. No defectless e*f assertion is used.

Define TH(v)=integral H dmu_v. The coefficient formula makes T continuous on the primary-gauged lattice, and density with ||T||<=n gives continuity on all continuous H. On -w(J)/k it returns -v(N(J))/k, so it preserves C by approximation. If u=h composed with restriction is fibre-constant, Tu=nh. A full finite fibre with positive weights permits decreasing limits, including bottom, to commute with this finite sum. Tracing an actual decreasing C_B-net therefore yields an actual decreasing C_A-net with limit h. This proves continuous and D-descent over normal domain targets.

For a reduced finite source with vertical components, trace ONLY its generic-dominating domain components and divide by the sum of their genuine generic degrees. Their boundaries cover the target by lying over. Full fibre constancy forces the same descended value also on vertical lifts. No canonical generic degree or unrestricted trace is invented for vertical components. General reduced-target descent uses normalization and reduced base change in later LOCAL proofs.

Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n4: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS. Use LOCAL n1--n3.

Fix epsilon>0. Choose j=-w(J)/k approximating u and kappa=-v(K)/k approximating h0 within epsilon, synchronize denominators and ensure 1/k<epsilon. A tiny negative primary correction makes J proper at positive-dimensional centres. On E the ideal-value difference is less than 2k epsilon. Choose positive L with 2k epsilon<L<=2k epsilon+1. Then Q=KE(aE)^L has w(Q)>=w(JE). Its positive primary factor gives Q-image zero on every zero-dimensional component where JE is nonunit. LOCAL n2 proves integral dependence on ALL components and one h' with Q^(N+h') contained in (JE)^N.

The actual proper primary ideals I_N=J^N intersect R contain powers of a. The conductor fibre product gives EXACTLY (I_N+c)/c=(JE)^N intersect C0: if x in J^N has residue coming from R/c, then x differs from an R-element by c subset R and therefore belongs to R. This is not arbitrary base-change contraction.

At infinite conductor the common exponent gives v(I_N)/(kN)<=(1+h'/N)(v(K)/k+L/k), evaluated on finite-valued quotient primary ideals. At finite conductor, the unique lift satisfies w(J)/k<=v(I_N)/(kN)<=w(J)/k+v(c)/(kN), since cJ^N subset I_N. That estimate is used ONLY where v(c) is finite. No infinity/N or uniform nonprimary-conductor bound appears.

Everywhere v(I_N)/(kN)>=-h-epsilon. The limiting upper bounds are -h+epsilon at finite conductor and at most -h+4epsilon at infinity. Since I_N^2 subset I_(2N), b_l=v(I_(2^l))/(k2^l) decreases. The increasing open sets {b_l+h<5epsilon} cover the compact boundary, so one covers it. Thus -b_l in Q_R uniformly approximates h. These negative profiles increase only INTERNALLY during approximation; this adds no increasing-limit operation to D. Letting epsilon decrease proves h in C_R.

For any reduced finite injection R -> B, set B'=(B tensor_R S)_red. S -> B' is injective: integral surjectivity on spectra survives base change, so the kernel lies in every prime of reduced S. All actual full fibres and proper primary ideals on nonempty local-centre factors survive. Pull back to B', descend over normal centres by n3, then descend S -> R by the normalization argument. Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n5: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS. Use LOCAL n1--n4.

Suppose fibre-constant u in D_S descends to strictly negative upper semicontinuous h, possibly unbounded and partially bottom. Compactness gives h<=-c for a FINITE c>0. All-bottom descends directly by -Nv(a). Normal targets use n3; normalization steps use dimension induction on the conductor quotient.

Given finite continuous F>h, the lower semicontinuous positive gap F-h has a positive compact lower bound. Even if its infimum is infinity, choose a finite e>0. A compact strict open-cover argument and directedness select ONE term g of the actual decreasing C_S representation with g<-c/2 and g<F composed with restriction-e/2. Choose b>0 with b||g||<e/8. Scaling to (1-b)g creates a uniform gap at least bc/2 above finite u. Rational approximation gives j=-w(J)/k with u+s<=j<F composed with restriction-e/8, for s>0. Bottom points satisfy the lower inequality automatically. Put M=||j||.

On the conductor quotient choose b1 with b1 M<s/4 and b1 sufficiently small. Since u<=j-s, the scaled target satisfies (1-b1)u<j-s/4; bottom causes no ambiguity. Compact selection from a decreasing representation of h0, followed by sufficiently accurate rational approximation, gives kappa=-v(K)/k>=h0 and its pullback <j_E+delta. Scaling the strictly negative quotient majorant provides the positive gap needed for the lower inequality. Synchronize denominators with 1/k<delta. Choose positive L with k delta<L<=k delta+1. Then Q=KE(aE)^L is integral over JE on ALL components, and n2 supplies the common exponent.

Exact contraction as in n4 yields an INTERNAL increasing dyadic family f_l=-v(I_(2^l))/(k2^l), bounded above by j. Its limiting lower bound is >=kappa-2delta>=h-2delta at infinity, and it tends to j>=h+s at finite conductor. The open sets {f_l>h-3delta} cover the compact boundary, including bottom points. Choose one finite f. Set eta=3delta/c, choosing delta so eta<1/2 and eta M<e/16. Then q=(1-eta)f belongs to C_R. At finite h<=-c,
(1-eta)(h-3delta)=h+eta(-h)-3delta+3delta eta>=h+3delta eta,
so q>h. At bottom any finite q is above h. Also q<=j+eta M<F. Thus h<q<F using positive scaling, not subtraction in D.

All strict C-majorants are downward directed by insertion below their minimum. Reverse pointwise order makes them an ACTUAL decreasing C_R-net. Its infimum is h: for any finite t>h(v), compact Hausdorff separation and upper semicontinuity provide finite continuous F>h with F(v)<t; insertion produces a C-majorant below F. This also handles h(v)=-infinity. The dimension induction therefore uses neither increasing closure nor unsupported flattening of nested nets.

Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n6: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS. Use LOCAL n1--n5.

For divisorial density on an excellent local DOMAIN, start with a supportful normalized v and a primary generator a0 with v(a0)=1. Adjoin all a_j/a0 to a finite-type birational chart B0. For finite positive coordinates v(f), choose rational bounds p/q<v(f)<r/s and adjoin f^q/a0^p and a0^r/f^s. For infinite coordinates impose only lower bounds. Every denominator has finite value, so evaluation uses the support quotient and its valued fraction field. The positive prime P contains a0 and the strict ratios and contracts to m. A Rees DVR of the excellent positive-dimensional B0_P satisfies these strict inequalities and nu(a)=nu(a0)>0. By n2's dimension and residue formulas, trdeg_k kappa(nu)=trdeg_k kappa(P)+dim(B0_P)-1=dim R-1. It is discrete rank one and divisorial in Rond--Spivakovsky's sense. Units and zero have their forced values. This proves all-support density without characteristic-zero resolution.

Now assume R normal. For fixed divisorial nu, n2 gives nu(f)<=C_nu ord_m(f) for nonunits; units are separate. Since v0(m)>=1/r, ord_m(f)<=r v0(f). Choosing an ideal generator of least finite v0-value gives nu(I)<=C_nu r v0(I). Thus a negative finite REAL profile satisfies g(nu)>=C_nu r g(v0), and the inequality passes to C. If g(v0)=0, nonpositivity forces g(nu)=0 for all divisorial nu; density and continuity give g=0. If a D-function vanishes at v0, every term of its decreasing C-net vanishes there and hence identically. Each normal-centre D-function is therefore either zero everywhere or strictly negative everywhere, possibly bottom at some points. Compactness bounds each nonzero centre above by a finite negative constant.

For normalization S, mark the finitely many active centre pieces where u is nonzero. Active and inactive pieces cannot share a fibre. The indicator sigma=-1 on active pieces and 0 elsewhere belongs to C_S by primary/unit Chinese-remainder gluing. Its fibre-constant descent lies in C_R BY n4's POSITIVE descent, not topology alone. T={sigma=-1} is clopen; h=0 off T and h<=-c on T for finite c>0. Empty T gives zero. If all active values are bottom, the decreasing sequence N sigma gives bottom there and exact zero elsewhere.

Generally, adding the negative constant -delta to u invokes n5 and gives h-delta in D_R. This does NOT authorize an increasing limit as delta tends to zero. Instead, for finite continuous F>h on T choose finite compact gap e, small eta with eta(||F||+e)<e/4, and delta=eta c/[2(1-eta)]. At finite active points,
(1-eta)(h-delta)=h+eta(-h-c/2)>h,
and the scaled target is below F-e/2; bottom remains bottom. Compact selection from the actual decreasing C-net for h-delta gives g with (1-eta)g<F-e/4 on T. Choose N with -N<min_T F and put q=max((1-eta)g,N sigma). Then q is in C_R, h<q<F on T, and q is EXACTLY zero off T because C-functions are nonpositive. Finite gaps and partial bottom survive.

These strict majorants with zero complement are downward directed by insertion below their minimum. Separation on compact T shows their infimum is h, yielding one ACTUAL decreasing C_R-net. Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n7: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS. Use LOCAL n1. The base is ACTUAL reduced excellent local R in positive dimension, without smoothness, normality, characteristic or perfect-field hypotheses.

R[It] is reduced as a subring of R[t]. Its maps to (R/p_i)[(I mod p_i)t] have prime kernels with zero intersection. Degree-zero component separators make these kernels incomparable; every prime contains one of them, so they are exactly the minimal primes. Each primary I-image is nonzero on a positive-dimensional component; its Proj dominates Spec(R/p_i). Hence Y_I has no extra vertical irreducible component. A generator f need not be regular in R, but its chart R[I/f] sits inside R_f, where f IS regular, and I O_Y=(f). Thus E is ACTUAL effective Cartier and -E is relatively ample. The model is projective and isomorphic away from m.

G1: Stacks 0B5S 30.16.1/3 makes T=H0(Y,O_Y) finite over R. Restriction of sections on reduced Y to its generic points injects T into product_i Frac(R/p_i)=Q(R), and birational dominance injects R into T. This is a GLOBAL embedding, not a map Q(R)->Frac(R/p) for supportful valuations. A finite affine cover with affine pairwise intersections computes H0 as a kernel of finite products; localization commutes with that kernel. Away from m, T localizes to R. Therefore T/R is finite and m-supported. If m^h(T/R)=0, the FIXED primary c0=m^(h+1) satisfies c0 T subset m AS ELEMENTS OF R.

G2: Stacks 01VG 29.38.4/5 identifies relative and absolute ampleness over the affine base. Stacks 01PR 28.27.13(7) generates A^(k-1)L for k large when A is ample. By 28.27.5, A^k L is ample; 28.27.2 supplies the required power-root rule. Y is Noetherian, quasicompact and separated, so all hypotheses hold.

G3: For integral ample A and integral curve-nef N, restrict to the FULL projective closed fibre X, possibly nonreduced and over an arbitrary residue field. Keeler corrected v5 Definition 2.9 uses degrees on integral curves. Its 5.19, derived from full 1.5, generates A^m N' uniformly for all nef N' once m is large. Take m=k-1 and N'=N^k. Then (AN)^k=A tensor a generated bundle is ample, and AN is ample by roots. Stacks 0D2N 30.21.4 lifts full-fibre ampleness near the closed point; that neighbourhood is the entire local base. Its full proof lifts high-power fibre sections, obtains generation, makes the projective map finite near the fibre and pulls back ampleness. No reduced-fibre assumption is present. Optional 01XO 30.17.5 proves nil-invariance, but is unnecessary.

The ENTIRE Keeler 2018 erratum was read. Old Lemma 3.3 is false. Correct E1.3 changes to a finite faithfully flat base with smooth geometrically integral fibres; E2.4 transfers vanishing, and E2.5 repairs 1.5. Consequently 1.5 and 5.19 survive without adding smoothness, normality, reducedness or algebraically closed residue-field hypotheses to our application.

For REAL perturbation, real ampleness means a finite positive real combination of ample integral classes in Pic(Y) tensor_Z REAL NUMBERS. Rational nef F plus integral ample A is genuinely Q-ample after clearing denominators, applying G3 and taking roots. A+tF for real t>=0 is real ample by bracketing t with nonnegative rational parameters. For real ample S=sum s_j A_j and rational nef F, with s=sum s_j, write S+F=sum s_j(A_j+F/s).

Let D=sum d_i L_i be REAL curve-nef and H integral ample. Choose N_i so N_i H +/-L_i are ample. Then |deg L_i|<=N_i deg H on every contracted curve. For rational delta>0 choose rational d'_i with e_i=d_i-d'_i and sum N_i|e_i|<delta/4. F=sum d'_i L_i+delta H/4 is rational nef. The residual

is explicitly real ample. Rational nef plus real ample proves D+delta H ample. For arbitrary positive real delta, first choose a smaller positive rational delta.

A+sum e_i L_i=(1-sum N_i|e_i|)A+sum |e_i|(N_i A+sign(e_i)L_i).
For a general positive ample combination, reserve part of one summand.

A Q-Cartier class that is real ample is genuinely Q-ample. Use only the FINITELY GENERATED subgroup G of Pic(Y) generated by its integral multiple and the finitely many ample summands.
